1. Project Overview

Event Celestial — Orientation Party 2024
Institution Taylor’s University
Role Lead Brand Designer
Scope Brand identity, design system, print, merch, art direction

Celestial was the official visual identity created for Taylor’s University Orientation Party 2024. The theme, “Where Stars Align,” was developed to visually and emotionally represent new beginnings, community, and the beautiful collision of different paths converging at Taylor’s.

Rather than designing isolated visuals, I built Celestial as a complete brand universe — one that lives across print, digital screens, physical event spaces, merchandise, and storytelling assets.

2. Creative Direction

Celestial’s identity was developed using three core design pillars that guided every element across all layouts and collateral.

Celestial Constellations

Constellations, star trails, planets, and comet-like strokes represent alignment — new friendships forming, students crossing paths, and unique stories meeting in one shared orbit.

Musical Motion

Floating musical notes symbolise celebration, rhythm, laughter, and the overall vibrancy of campus life. These elements visually express performance energy and youth culture.

Futuristic Glow

Gradients, glow effects, nebula-like shading, and metallic typography create a dreamy, modern fantasy atmosphere — fitting for a night that marks the beginning of a new academic journey.

Together, these principles shaped an environment that feels magical, immersive, and full of hope.

3. Main Logo Design

The Main Logo reflects the cosmic essence of Celestial. Its composition includes planet rings, orbital trails, sparks, and musical accents, all orbiting the word “Celestial.”

Design considerations included strong central radiance to symbolise unity, starburst marks to create motion, musical notes as delicate decorative details, and elegant typography with a slight fantasy touch.

The logo was designed to scale seamlessly across large hall banners, LED screens, print tickets, merchandise, badges, and small icon placements. The final design maintains high clarity at any size and instantly communicates the spirit of the event.

4. Design Assets System

The design assets were created as modular building blocks to ensure consistency across all event materials.

  • Planets & Sparks
  • Orbit lines & Music notes
  • Event-specific symbols

These graphical components enabled dynamic compositions without breaking the brand language. Every poster, card, signage, sticker, and UI screen remained visually consistent within the same universe.

5. Characters Card Design

The Characters Card Design focuses on the main characters of the Celestial orientation storyline, each representing their own planet and personality.

Each card features planetary identity tied to the character, distinct traits hinting at persona roles, custom-framed layouts for recognisability, and orbit elements that strengthen the cosmic theme.

These cards were more than visuals — they acted as a storytelling platform, turning the event into a narrative experience where students could recognise and follow central figures.

Every card followed the same Celestial aesthetic: cosmic glow, star spark textures, planetary naming system, and consistent card architecture. They became signature artefacts that anchored the event’s visual storytelling.

6. Poster Designs

The Poster Designs provided navigational clarity while fully immersing students in the Celestial visual world.

Posters included the Main Event Poster, Ticket Collection Poster, Dinner Collection Poster, Stamp Rally Redemption Counter, and Directional Sign Posters.

The design approach used layered cosmic backgrounds, high-contrast typographic layouts, metallic-white typography for legibility, and constellations and orbit strokes framing key information.

These posters ensured students could navigate the event easily while remaining inside the fantasy universe.

7. Team Logo Designs

To distinguish team roles behind the event, Team Logo Designs were created with thematic consistency and colour-coded identity. Teams included Orientation Party, Flashmob, Deco, Shooting, and Characters Team.

Each circular logo preserved Celestial’s core asset styling, typography treatment, and orbit-inspired composition. These logos were applied on crew identity markers, shirt stamps, lanyard symbols, and internal branding communication. They created pride, belonging, and structure among the organising teams.

8. T-Shirt Designs

The T-Shirt Designs extended the brand into wearable identity. Two colourways were developed: Celestial Blue and Cosmic White.

Each shirt integrates the main logo back print, orbit trail graphics, character universe illustrations, themed typography, spark lights, and starbursts.

These shirts became unity wear, creating instant connection between attendees, crew members, and student leaders.

9. Photostrips Design

The Photostrips Design turned photography sessions into a fully branded experience using star textures, planet symbols, orbital frames, and musical accents. Students took home photos that visually tied back to the Celestial universe. As a high-traffic activity, the identity became instantly recognisable across social media.

10. Ticket Design

The Ticket Design reflected the event’s elegance and exclusivity. It included the programme title, venue and timing, spark trails, orbit frames, and tagline placement. The tickets also doubled as memory tokens, with many students keeping them after the event.

11. Sticker Design

The Sticker Designs applied branding into small-scale collectibles used for thank-you gifts, crew packs, event rewards, and personal mementos. They emphasised the Celestial mark, glowing textures, and orbital compositions. These became small but powerful brand reinforcements throughout the event.

12. Lanyard Design

The Lanyard Design featured the event name, spark motifs, planet iconography, and the tagline “Where Stars Align.” Different versions were created for internal crew, external guests, and alumni. Colour variations preserved hierarchy while maintaining brand unity.

13. Wristband Design

The Wristband Design carried repeating music notes, spark lines, and the logotype. It functioned as admission control while staying fully branded.

14. Website Queuing Page Design

A fully branded Website Queuing Page was designed to extend the Celestial identity into the digital experience.

It includes student ID input and search, queue status, confirmation icons, capacity indicator bar, and a cosmic gradient background.

This ensured Celestial existed not only physically, but digitally as well.

15. Design Outcomes

The Celestial identity successfully unified the entire event into one shared visual language.

✦ Recognisable brand presence
✦ Immersive thematic visuals
✦ Character-driven storytelling
✦ Memorable keepsakes

"Celestial didn’t just decorate an orientation party. It built a world around it."

16. Reflection

Designing Celestial taught me that branding becomes powerful when it carries meaning. Every spark stroke, every card frame, every gradient tone had a purpose — to make new students feel welcomed, excited, and connected to something bigger than themselves.

Through this project, I strengthened my skills in brand system building, collateral consistency, thematic world-building, narrative character styling, and large-scale event identity application.

Celestial was not just a theme. It became an experience.

The Orientation Leaders Yearbook 24/25 📖

The Orientation Leaders Yearbook 24/25, a fully designed and developed website that documents the memories, achievements, and journey of the Orientation Leaders community across 2024 & 2025. This yearbook was built for the Taylor's Orientation Leaders under Taylor's University — a student body committed to welcoming new students and host orientation events for freshmen.

🚀 Project Origin & Execution

"This project started as a simple idea: ‘How can we preserve our stories in a meaningful, interactive, and accessible way?’"

From there, I took on the responsibility of bringing it to life — from concept, content structure, layout planning, UI/UX design, front-end development, media organization, and final deployment. I ideated and executed the entire project lifecycle, including:

✅
UX Research & Information Architecture

Structuring content flow, identifying user needs, and planning intuitive navigation for a community-focused platform.

✅
UI/UX Design (Figma)

All pages, layouts, color palettes, typography, spacing systems, and components were designed from scratch using Figma. Every design decision was driven by readability, hierarchy, and emotional storytelling to create a warm, community focused experience.

✅
Front-End Development

Building the website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, implementing responsive layouts, media components, hover interactions, and custom UI behaviors.

🚧 Challenges & How I Overcame Them

Challenge 1 Balancing emotional storytelling with functional clarity

Yearbooks are nostalgic, but websites must still be clean and usable. Too much decoration would hurt readability; too little would reduce emotional impact.

Solution

I designed with clarity first principles — using hierarchy, white space, and structured layouts — while adding subtle emotional cues through warm colors, gentle shadows, and media-first components to preserve the “memory” feeling.

Challenge 2 Creating responsive layouts for media-heavy pages

Many sections contain photo grids and long messages, which behave differently on desktop and mobile.

Solution

I prototyped multiple responsive patterns in Figma, tested breakpoints, and built flexible CSS grid structures to ensure every gallery, card, and section maintained its visual balance across screens.

🧠 Design Strategy & Visual Direction

The overall visual direction of the Orientation Leaders Yearbook 24/25 was guided by three core principles: clarity, warmth, and emotional storytelling. As the platform serves both current students and alumni, the interface needed to feel professional yet personal.

A card-based system was adopted to present leadership profiles, events, and recognition highlights. This structure allows content to be digested easily while maintaining visual consistency throughout the website. Soft shadows, balanced spacing, and controlled animation were applied to enhance depth without overwhelming the user.

The typography system was carefully selected to ensure strong readability across long content sections, while the color palette reinforces a warm, community-driven identity that reflects leadership, teamwork, and celebration.

🗂 Information Architecture & Content Flow

The website was structured to mirror the real journey of an Orientation Leader:

Introduction & Identity

Who the Orientation Leaders are.

Leadership Recognition

EXCO & BOD structure.

Events & Engagement

Activities throughout the term.

Recognition & Achievements

Wall of Fame.

Memories & Visual Archive

Gallery.

This structure ensures users experience the website as a story, not just a collection of pages. The flow transitions naturally from structure → action → recognition → memory.

💻 Front-End Implementation Highlights

The website was fully developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with focus on:

Fully responsive grid-based layouts
Interactive hover states for profile and event cards
Smooth scrolling behavior for long content pages
Optimized image handling for media-heavy sections
Consistent animation timing for professional UI feedback

Every interaction was tested across desktop, tablet, and mobile to ensure consistent behavior and performance.

📊 Project Impact & Outcomes

  • ✓

    Successfully created a permanent digital archive for Taylor’s Orientation Leaders

  • ✓

    Strengthened leadership brand presence and recognition

  • ✓

    Increased accessibility for alumni and future leaders

  • ✓

    Served as a public-facing leadership & culture showcase

  • ✓

    Demonstrated a full UI/UX + Front-End workflow in one complete project

"This platform now stands as both a community legacy project and a professional portfolio-grade web product."

🎯 Personal Growth & Learning Outcomes

Through this project, I strengthened my ability to:

Design emotionally driven UI while maintaining usability Build large-scale content websites independently Balance leadership storytelling with functional clarity Handle long-term project planning and execution Translate community identity into a meaningful digital experience

This yearbook was not just a design project — it was a real product built for real people, which made the experience deeply meaningful and professionally valuable.

"Although I developed the platform myself, this yearbook wouldn’t exist without everyone who contributed content, photos, stories, and feedback. This project reminded me how meaningful it is to design for a real community, not just a grade or assignment. I’m grateful for the support and contributions who helped make this possible, and I look forward to applying these skills to future design and development projects."

Visit Live Website 🚀

1. Overview

MyTIMES is the official academic platform used in Taylor’s University for accessing learning materials, announcements, quizzes, submissions, and lecture recordings. However, continuous student feedback revealed strong frustration with cluttered layouts, poor navigation hierarchy, and inefficient access to core academic tools.

This redesign project focuses on solving real student workflow problems through a structured UX methodology involving research, data analysis, information architecture, Lo-Fi prototyping, Hi-Fi interface design, and user testing.

2 Research Insights & Core Pain Points

PAIN POINTS
Identified Issues
  • ✕ Slow navigation caused by deep and unstructured menus
  • ✕ Materials and recordings scattered across multiple layers
  • ✕ Completed and upcoming tasks mixed together
  • ✕ Calendar feature hidden and underused
  • ✕ Discussions not placed in meaningful learning context
SOLUTIONS
Top User Needs
  • ✓ Shortest possible path to active or recently accessed courses
  • ✓ One-glance visibility of tasks and deadlines
  • ✓ Clear separation between completed and pending work
  • ✓ Calendar placed on primary navigation
  • ✓ Strong content hierarchy inside every course module
Draft Proposal
Application Design Mobile Application Draft Proposal by Icese

3 UX Goals

1
Faster Access

Recently used courses should appear at the top of the dashboard for instant resume learning.

2
Content Structure

Files, lecture videos, quizzes, and assignments must be grouped into clear, separated tabs.

3
Intelligent Calendar

Calendar must be exposed on the main navigation with repeat scheduling and category support.

4
Contextual Discussion

Discussion panels should be placed directly under recordings for natural class-based interaction.

📙 Final Proposal (Refined UX Strategy & Structure)

Open Proposal in Canva ↗

4. Information Architecture

Simplified Course Structure
Materials
Recordings
Quizzes
Assignments
Discussion
Bottom Navigation
Home | Courses | Calendar | Notifications | Profile

"This structure ensures that all essential academic tools are reachable in under two taps."

5. Before vs After Comparison

A. Dashboard (Before)
  • ❌ Displays full course listing repeatedly
  • ❌ Recently accessed courses hidden behind multiple taps
  • ❌ No prioritisation of active learning
After Redesign
  • ✅ “Recently Accessed” placed at the very top
  • ✅ Full course list remains available but secondary
  • ✅ Faster resume learning flow
Result: Significant reduction in taps and search time.
B. Materials, Recordings & Activities
  • ❌ All mixed into one unclear content list
  • ❌ High confusion and slow retrieval
After Redesign
  • ✅ Clear tab separation: Materials, Recordings, Quizzes, Assignments
  • ✅ Workflow follows real academic usage pattern
Result: Faster retrieval, reduced cognitive load, better clarity.
C. Quizzes & Assignments

Before: Mixed together, no progress awareness

After: Two-column structure (Upcoming vs Completed), visual toning

Result: Better planning, clearer motivation, improved deadline awareness.

D. Calendar

Before: Hidden inside sub-menus, rarely used

After: Main nav position, color coding, 5-day preview

Result: Calendar becomes an active planning tool instead of a hidden feature.

6. Visual UI Explanation Panels

1
Dashboard Layout

Design Logic: Recently Accessed placed at top for fastest resume. Full course list remains below. High contrast typography supports categorisation.

Impact: Users immediately know where to look and what to tap.

2
Class Folder Structure

Design Logic: Strict separation between Materials, Recordings, and Activities. Folder visuals clearly separated. Larger touch zones.

Impact: Students locate files, videos, and submissions without unnecessary exploration.

3
Assignment & Quiz Two-Column Layout

Design Logic: Reflects mental priority of upcoming tasks. Completed tasks visually greyed. Urgent tasks highlighted.

Impact: Students gain instant awareness of deadlines and progress completion.

4
Discussion Panel Placement

Design Logic: Discussions anchored directly under recordings for context-based interaction after lecture viewing.

Impact: Academic engagement becomes purposeful instead of scattered.

7. User Testing (Condensed)

Validated Improvements
  • Users resumed learning faster through Recently Accessed
  • Lecture recordings became discoverable with one tap
  • Completed task separation strongly clarified progress tracking
  • Calendar became a desired daily planning feature
Suggestions Addressed
  • Calendar color coding
  • Clearer notification categorisation
🧪 User Testing Embed
Open User Testing in Canva

8. UI/UX Documentation

A full UI/UX document was created to support long-term scalability and implementation consistency. It includes: Design system (colors, typography, components), Interaction behaviours, Screen flows and transitions, User journey mapping, and Edge case logic.

📄 Full UI/UX System Documentation

Interactive embed of the design system standards and guidelines.

View Document ↗

9. Lo-Fi & Hi-Fi Prototypes

Explore the interactive Figma prototypes below.

🧩 Lo-Fi Prototype
🎨 Hi-Fi Prototype

10. Final Outcome

The redesigned MyTIMES platform achieved:

  • ✦ Reduced navigation steps
  • ✦ Clear discovery of core academic tools
  • ✦ Improved content hierarchy
  • ✦ Higher engagement through contextual features
  • ✦ Lower cognitive overload

Post-testing sentiment reflected noticeable improvements in clarity, efficiency, and usability.

11. Reflection

This redesign transformed MyTIMES from a functional but cluttered academic system into a structured, fast, and context-driven learning platform.

UX Maturity

Clear information architecture, Strong user-goal alignment, Research-driven decisions, Usability validation, Iterative design improvement.

VerdeHome is a smart home energy management application designed to help users monitor, control, and optimise their home energy, water, and gas usage in real time. The app focuses on making sustainability simple, visual, and actionable for everyday users.

Interactive Storybook

Winnie the Pooh

"A childhood story that carries warmth, simplicity, friendship, and adventure."

1

Project Overview

This project required the creation of a thematic interactive website built around an original concept. I chose Winnie the Pooh to translate the charm of the Hundred Acre Wood into a digital experience that encourages users to explore, learn, and interact through playful animations.

Rather than building a static layout, I created a site that behaves like a moving storybook: characters animate, items respond to clicks, timelines reveal history, and maps invite discovery.

Procreate Asset Creation
Adobe Animate Interactive Scripting
Figma Wireframes
Web Host Fully Published
2

Design Concept

Hand-Drawn Doodle Style

All trees, characters, and icons were hand-illustrated in Procreate. The goal was authenticity—ensuring the website feels like it belongs in Pooh’s universe.

Soft Storybook Colours

Pastel greens, wood-tone browns, cotton-sky blues, and warm yellows create a gentle, nostalgic mood.

Child-Friendly Interaction

Animations are simple, optimistic, and curious—mirroring Pooh’s personality. The site is comforting and whimsical.

3

Key Features & Interactive Elements

🌳 Loading Animation
  • ☁️ Elements fade out one by one
  • 🎈 Balloon rises to the sky
  • ⏳ Loading bar animates from 0–100%
Tech: Shape Tweens, Layer-separated timeline, Delayed animations.
🧸 Home Page — Character Greeting

The homepage opens like a story cover. Title letters appear with drop motion tweening, and Tigger performs a jump animation triggered by JavaScript logic (Velocity & bounce height).

"This interaction encourages discovery instead of static clicking."

📜 Interactive History Page

A horizontally animated timeline of Winnie the Pooh’s evolution (1920–2022). Each card slides in, pauses, and enlarges on hover.

Interaction: Next button reveals eras until "Begin the Adventure" pops up.
🐾 Adventure Journey Pages

Users help the characters walk towards a destination. Characters travel with timed horizontal motion using tweens, reflecting story progression.

"This section turns interaction into a mini-quest."

🗺 Interactive Map
  • Hand-drawn map of the forest
  • Clickable character houses
  • Detailed character cards on click
  • Transitions to Disney Store
🛍 Web Store Page

A small themed shop displaying stickers, plushies, and items. Navigation integrates with frame-label actions for smooth transitions back to the Map or Home.

4

Research & Inspiration

Studied highly interactive sites on The FWA like The Silly Bunny and Snoopy x Evian. This guided the focus on:

Storytelling through interaction Movement triggered by navigation Clickable discovery maps Immersive environments
5

Development Pipeline

✦ Asset Creation (Procreate)

Every tree, path, cloud, and and character icon was self-drawn. This ensured no copyright conflicts and perfect thematic unity.

✦ Wireframes (Figma)

Rough UX skeleton showing layout, navigation, and card overlays. Helped ensure simplicity before styling.

✦ Logic Flow Chart

Mapped out journey logic: Home → History → Adventure → Map → Character → Store.

6

UI/UX Design Goals

📖
Storytelling "Walk through" Pooh's world.
🧠
Learning History in scroll-based reveal.
🧭
Exploration Choose where to go.
💖
Emotion Innocence & nostalgia.
👆
Interaction Click, hover, press, reveal.

7. Final Outcome

🚀 Visit Live Website 🎬 Watch Demo Video 🧰 View Figma Prototype

8. Reflections

Personal Experience

This was my first time combining custom asset illustration, animation keyframing, and interactive coding. Learning Adobe Animate from zero was challenging, but watching my own illustrated characters come to life was incredibly rewarding.

Observations
  • Interactivity only works well when navigation is clear
  • Keyframe pacing changes how characters “feel”
  • Animation should support usability, not distract from it

9. Final Thoughts

This project was a nostalgic journey and a growth process in animation and UX structuring. Bringing Pooh, Piglet, Tigger, and Eeyore to life through digital interaction felt magical.

"The site proves that even the simplest stories can become immersive if designed through the lens of UX, motion, narrative, and exploration."

4.1 Landing Page

Greets visitors with emotional messaging. UX Intent: Showcase quality instantly and create emotional appetite.

4.2 Best Sellers Showcase

Displays popular desserts to entice visitors and nudge intent. Encourage deeper browsing with "See More".

4.3 Special Orders Section

Introduces custom celebration cakes. CTA: Place an Order — a direct path for high-intent customers.

4.5 Product Menu Pages

Simple categorization (Whole Cakes, Beverages, Specials). Green "Order Now" buttons trigger action psychologically.

4.8 Special Order Form Page

Functional heart of the site. Collects specific details (Flavor, Delivery, Zip Code) in an extended, distraction-free layout.

UX Design Intent

Emotional Comfort: Friendly, handwritten typography, nostalgic feel.

Simplicity: Clear navigation (Products, About, Contact). Small brands thrive on clarity.

Conversion: Subconscious guide from Browsing -> Trust -> Category -> Order.

Form Handling

The special order form is crucial. Its layout maximizes clarity while maintaining tone. Large fields reduce friction.

Establishes professionalism, buyer confidence, and a simple communication pipeline.

Outcome & Reflection

Project Strengths
  • ✔ Brand identity clearly reflected
  • ✔ Soft and approachable tone
  • ✔ Structured product menu
  • ✔ Contact systems ready for real use

"Designing Bake Diary helped me explore how visual character can shape a brand’s personality. I learned that bakery brands are successful when their design communicates the same care and sincerity as their products."

Type Design Case Study

Heaventh Typeface

Type Exploration, Font Development & Commercial Application

Project Overview

Heaventh is a custom display typeface developed through an in-depth exploration of letterform structure, stylistic consistency, and real-world application. The project focused on studying an existing visual style, improving its weaknesses, expanding it into a full alphabet system, and deploying it across commercial merchandise and promotional media.

The goal was to transform a concept-based typographic style into a fully functional, exportable typeface (.TTF) that maintains strong identity, readability, and commercial usability.

Concept & Direction

1

Album-Inspired

A font expansion based on the visual style of the album Seventeenth Heaven by Seventeen — energetic, youthful, expressive, and street-inspired. The original lettering lacked a complete alphabet, presenting a strong opportunity for full type development.

2

Tiger-Inspired

A concept rooted in the visual strength and elegance of tigers using elements such as stripes, claws, and motion.

"Energetic. Youthful. Bold Movement."

After conceptual review, the album-inspired direction was selected due to its strong identity potential, originality, and cultural relevance.

Uppercase Letterform Development

Initial sketch exploration focused on developing expressive uppercase characters from A–Z. During this phase, a defining visual feature emerged:

Thick terminal ends and small stroke knots were introduced to give the font a bold, playful, and energetic character.

Once refined, the sketches were digitised in Adobe Illustrator while maintaining the expressive characteristics of the hand-drawn forms.

Structural Consistency

Early digitisation revealed inconsistencies in stroke width, curve angles, and proportions. To correct this, a benchmark system was introduced using the letter “E” as the core reference structure.

  • Standardised stroke width
  • Unified curve angles
  • Proportional balancing

This transformed the font from expressive sketches into a cohesive, professional alphabet system.

Lowercase Development

Lowercase letter design followed the same systemisation logic. Selected lowercase letters were derived directly from uppercase structures to maintain stylistic harmony.

Numbers & Punctuation

Designing numbers and punctuation required translating the same visual DNA into functional symbols. Several early designs lacked stylistic integration and were restructured to match stroke thickness and terminal characteristics.

123 !?.

Font Engineering

The completed characters were imported into FontLab 8 for full font construction.

Kerning Tracking Side Bearings

Full sentence testing ensured smooth real-world readability.

Visual Presentation

Commercial Applications

Merch

Banner

Poster

Stickers

Apparel

Ready to Use?

✨ Uppercase ✨ Lowercase ✨ Kerning ✨ .TTF
Download Heaventh Typeface

Experience

This project strengthened my ability to manage large-scale typographic systems and execute a font from concept to distribution. The process sharpened both my creative intuition and technical discipline.

Key Takeaway

"Typeface design demands absolute consistency. A single variation in stroke weight or spacing can weaken the entire system."

projects.details:
Typography System Design

Structured Typographic Composition | Visual Hierarchy | Grid-Based Layout Exploration

1. Project Overview

This project explores how typography can be structured using different typographic systems to create order, hierarchy, rhythm, and visual clarity. Instead of treating text as simple content, the goal was to use typography as the primary design structure — where alignment, spacing, balance, and flow define the composition.

Eight Core Typographic Systems Explored
Axial Radial Dilatational Random Grid Modular Transitional Bilateral

All designs were developed within a controlled visual constraint of black plus one accent color, using only typography and minimal graphic elements. This helped maintain focus on structural layout rather than decoration.

2. Research & System Understanding

Before designing, I studied how each typographic system functions structurally and visually:

Axial

Organises text around a central axis to create balance and order.

Radial

Radiates elements outward from a focal point.

Dilatational

Expands typography outward in circular or layered motion.

Random

Breaks traditional structure to create energy and unpredictability.

Grid

Uses columns and rows to enforce strict alignment.

Modular

Organises text into repeated visual units.

Transitional

Applies traditional reading flow with subtle structural changes.

Bilateral

Mirrors text symmetrically across a central axis.

3. Concept Development & Sketching

Before digital execution, each typographic system was first explored through hand sketches. These early sketches focused on: Alignment direction, Spatial division, Visual balance, Reading flow, and Negative space.

Sketching allowed quick experimentation with layout structures before refining them digitally.

4. Digital Design Process

Each system was digitally constructed with its own unique composition logic.

Axial System

Typography was aligned along a strong central axis. Visual depth was created through layered rectangular elements and offset shadows. One composition explored diagonal tension while another focused on controlled symmetry. The final direction emphasized clarity, balance, and depth.

Radial System

Text elements were arranged to radiate outward from a central focal point using circular forms. Initial explorations focused on dense layering before refining toward a cleaner, more focused radial spread to strengthen visual impact and legibility.

Dilatational System

Overlapping circular forms were used to simulate expansion and motion. The composition creates a sense of space and depth by allowing text to visually “breathe” outward from the center.

Random System

The layout intentionally breaks structure. Letter angles, scale, spacing, and alignment were varied to generate disorder, tension, and visual energy. Color and opacity were used to guide hierarchy while maintaining chaos.

Grid System

This design applied a strict column-based structure. All information was aligned precisely within grid units, creating a clean, editorial-style composition. Adjustments were made to ensure text never collided with structural lines.

Modular System

Typography was organised into repeated modules. The design balances structure and flexibility. After refinement, alignment and spacing were standardised for visual clarity and consistency.

Transitional System

This system focused on traditional reading flow with subtle visual emphasis. Color and spacing were used to highlight hierarchy while maintaining a calm, minimal aesthetic.

Bilateral System

The final composition mirrored text symmetrically across a central vertical axis. Balance and harmony were the primary design focus, refined to avoid harsh angles and improve visual stability.

5. Final Outcome & Reflection

The completed typography system demonstrates strong control of Alignment, Hierarchy, White space, Rhythm, Visual balance, and Structural logic. Each system maintains its unique spatial identity while still belonging to a cohesive typographic language.

Reflection
  • ✦ Design with structure before decoration
  • ✦ Use alignment as a storytelling tool
  • ✦ Control readability through spacing
  • ✦ Build flexible grid systems
  • ✦ Translate theoretical layout systems into practical design applications

"This typography system now serves as a foundational framework for editorial, poster, and UI layout design."

projects.details:
Expressive Typography

Type as Visual Expression | Conceptual Typography Design

1. Research & Visual Exploration

This project began with an exploration into the concept of type expression, where typography is used not just for readability, but as a visual language to communicate meaning, emotion, and action. In expressive typography, letters themselves become part of the visual narrative.

To develop a stronger understanding of this approach, I studied multiple typography expression references and analysed how designers manipulate scale, weight, spacing, and structure to visually represent motion, sound, and illusion.

Key Typography Principles Identified

Through this research, several essential principles emerged as critical in effective expressive typography:

Typeface Selection

Fonts must remain readable while supporting the emotional tone of the word.

Variation of Weight & Style

Using bold, light, and italic styles creates contrast, depth, and hierarchy.

Scale & Emphasis

Large and small letter variations help communicate dominance, motion, pressure, or softness.

These principles became the foundation of all design development.

2. Concept Selection & Ideation

From a broader list of possible words, I selected four words that could be powerfully expressed using typography alone:

Roar Chop Dive Illusion

Each word was chosen based on its ability to visually communicate sound, motion, or perception using only letterforms. I began with freehand ideation sketches, allowing form experimentation without limitations.

The early sketches were then refined with clearer visual logic, stronger typographic structure, and improved compositional clarity before transitioning into digital exploration.

3. Digitisation & Design Development

All designs were digitally developed with close attention to scale control, alignment, clipping, distortion, and visual balance. Each word went through multiple iterations to test how different typographic treatments could strengthen meaning.

A. ROAR — Expressing Sound & Power

Roar explores the visual representation of sound intensity and aggression.

Roar Variation 1

Typeface: Futura Std Light. The letter R is placed horizontally. Letters O, A, R increase progressively in size. This creates a visual build-up of sound energy.

Roar Variation 2

Combination of Futura Std Bold and Light. “R” and “A R” are separated to allow space for “O”. The “O” increases in stroke weight to imply deep vibration and resonance.

Roar Variation 3

Typeface: Futura Std Bold and Light. An oversized “O” placed at the centre. Surrounding “A” letters face inward like sharp teeth. A second inner “O” adds visual depth. The word transforms into a roaring mouth.

B. CHOP — Expressing Impact & Cutting Motion

Chop focuses on sudden force, separation, and physical impact.

Chop Variation 1

Typeface: ITC New Baskerville Std Roman. The word “CHOP-CHOP” is duplicated. A clipping mask splits the typography into two equal halves. This visually simulates the act of chopping.

Chop Variation 2

Overlapping duplicate words. The lower section hangs downward. This creates the illusion of gravity and separation after impact.

Chop Variation 3

Two overlapping “CHOP” words are cut in half. The lower half is slightly shifted to the right. This reinforces motion and directional force.

C. DIVE — Expressing Descent & Water Motion

Dive explores vertical movement, depth, and underwater atmosphere.

Dive Variation 1

Typeface: ITC Garamond Std Light Condensed. A large hollow “D” becomes a visual container. Repeated dot elements from the letter “i” form rising bubbles. The composition suggests underwater depth.

Dive Variation 2

Typeface: Baskerville Regular. Repeated dot patterns rise upward to simulate continuous bubbles.

Dive Variation 3

The letter “V” is duplicated and rotated. It forms a sharp downward motion. The letter “E” is rotated and attached beneath, enhancing the falling effect.

D. ILLUSION — Expressing Visual Deception

Illusion focuses on misdirection, repetition, and visual distortion.

Illusion Variation 1

Typeface: Futura Std Book and Light. Mixed uppercase and lowercase for height consistency. Shadow and vertical distortions create an optical illusion effect.

Illusion Variation 2

Typeface: Futura Std Medium. Circular “type on path” used repeatedly. Typography radiates outward in layers, creating depth and motion illusion.

Final Refinement
  • • Vertical lines replaced with the letter “L”
  • • Mixed uppercase and lowercase enhanced readability
  • • Gaps added intentionally to strengthen the illusion effect

The final result balances clarity with surreal distortion.

4. Motion Exploration — Illusion Animation

Among the four words, Illusion was selected for motion development. A sequence of 76 individual frames was created to gradually transform the typography over time.

These frames were assembled into an animation that reinforces:

  • ✦ Visual transformation
  • ✦ Spatial distortion
  • ✦ Depth perception
  • ✦ The transition from stability to illusion

This motion study extends the project beyond static typography into time-based visual expression.

5. Final Outcome

The completed works successfully demonstrate:

  • • Expressive typography built entirely from letterforms
  • • Strong communication without the use of illustrations
  • • Visual meaning driven by scale, rhythm, weight, and spatial control
  • • The ability to translate sound, motion, impact, and illusion into typographic form

Each word communicates not only through reading, but through visual perception.

6. Reflection & Learning Outcomes

Through this project, I strengthened my ability to:
  • • Treat typography as a storytelling medium, not just a text tool
  • • Translate abstract concepts such as sound and motion into visual form
  • • Apply hierarchy, contrast, and balance at a professional level
  • • Develop multiple design directions through iteration
  • • Build motion through frame-based transformation

"This project reshaped how I think about type — not as static text, but as a living visual language."

Final Result

projects.details:
Creative Letter-form Poster

Type Extraction | Organic Typography | Image & Letter Interplay

1. Project Overview

This project explores how letterforms can be extracted from real-world objects and transformed into expressive typography. Instead of starting from a traditional font, the process begins with visual observation, turning physical shapes into typographic structure.

Object of Exploration: French Fries

Chosen for their unique visual qualities:

Irregular edges Organic shapes Natural imperfections Playful character

These qualities made them ideal for creating a unique typographic identity.

2. Image Study & Letter Discovery

The first stage involved identifying potential letter shapes within the fries image. Using vector tools, natural contours were traced to extract possible letter structures.

The goal was to retain the visual identity of the fries while forming readable letters.

3. Typeface Alignment & Refinement

A classical serif typeface was selected as a proportional reference to guide stroke thickness, contrast, letter width, and structural consistency.

Refinement Process
  • ✦ Organic imperfection vs Legibility
  • ✦ Visual consistency vs Structural harmony

At later stages, zig-zag strokes and irregular edges were introduced deliberately to reinforce the natural fries texture.

4. Letter Development

Final Letters: L E T I H

Each letter maintains a shared structural rhythm and controlled stroke consistency, while celebrating the natural irregularity inspired by the fries.

5. Poster Design & Visual Interplay

After completing the custom type design, the letterforms were applied into a movie poster composition. The initial horror concept was later refined into a lighthearted comedy theme, allowing the playful nature of the fries to drive the emotional tone.

Key Refinements
Color matching between typography and fries
Image overlays on letter surfaces
Grain texture blending
Shadow control for realism

6. Final Poster Outcome

The final poster successfully demonstrates seamless interaction between image and typography. The organic type maintains readability while strengthening the visual storytelling driven by material texture.

Playful tone aligned with the subject matter.

7. Reflection

This project strengthened my ability to extract typography from real-world forms and design type without relying on existing fonts. It taught me how to balance organic imperfection with precision and integrate custom type into full visual compositions.

"It reinforced how type can exist as both text and object — becoming a bridge between image and communication."
